citation: Wood engraving 'McVicker's Theater' in A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, vol. 2 (Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885), p. 598.
author: unsigned engraver for A. T. Andreas
describes_date: 1857-1871: the theatre on Madison Street between State and Dearborn as built in 1857, before its remodelling of 1871
repository: Internet Archive, item historyofchicago02andr (printed page 598, leaf n623 of the scan).
locator: p. 598, top of the page, captioned 'McVicker's Theater': the theatre's Madison Street front and long side from across the street, four storeys of brick with corniced hoods over the windows, 'McVICKER'S THEATRE' lettered under a bracketed cornice, a belvedere with its own cornice and a flagstaff over the middle, an iron colonnade carrying a railed balcony across the ground storey, a two-storey frame neighbour with a false front (SANDS PALE CREAM ALE), a horse car in the street.
rights_note: Published 1885 in the United States; public domain.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-28 (T-3804) from the Internet Archive's page image of p. 598 (historyofchicago02andr, page n623). Not committed; forms read from it, no pixels sampled and no geometry traced.
note: The 1857 building. Andreas (p. 599) says the theatre was rebuilt inside in 1871 so that 'nothing but the walls of the old theater remained', reopening on 29 August 1871; the front's walls stood as drawn, its porch and belvedere in 1871 are not shown by any picture found.
what_it_supplies: the theatre's front: storeys, window hoods, lettered cornice, belvedere, ground-storey colonnade and balcony
that it stood among brick blocks and frame shops on Madison Street
what_it_does_not_supply: measured sizes or the front's width
